testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a law enforcement officer asks you to take a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) test:

options.text: You can refuse but must pay a $50 fine.
You will lose your CDL if you refuse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will lose your CDL if you refuse.
questions.explanation: Most states have an Implied Consent Law. By driving on state roads, you agree to take a drug or alcohol test if an officer asks. If you refuse, you lose your driving privileges. Learn the laws for every state where you drive.

questions.question: When using a mirror, you should:

options.text: Stare at it for a long time.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors with quick glances. Looking too long at a mirror means you are not watching the road ahead, and you can travel far without seeing what is coming.

questions.question: Mirrors should:

options.text: Only be used when entering a highway.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you stay aware of other traffic and watch for problems with your own vehicle.

questions.question: When stopping, you should apply the brake pedal by:
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. Gradual braking helps you maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Safer than talking on the phone.
About as safe as talking on the phone.
More distracting than talking on the phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: More distracting than talking on the phone.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more distracting than talking on the phone. It takes your mind off driving, requires you to take your hands off the wheel to type, and forces you to look away from the road.

questions.question: When pulled off on the side of the road:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When must you check cargo securement after starting a trip?
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting your trip, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured throughout the trip.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead:

options.text: Gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
Is not encouraged because it distracts you.
Is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Always watch for hazards ahead. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: If convicted of a traffic violation, you must tell your employer:
questions.explanation: If convicted of any traffic violation, notify your employer within 30 days. Also notify your licensing agency within 30 days if it happened in another state. Parking tickets do not count.

questions.question: What must happen before air pressure in an air brake system falls below 55 psi?

options.text: The vehicle will be unable to shift out of gear.

questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light must activate before the air supply drops below 55 psi. If the warning does not activate during inspection, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: Before each trip, you should inspect your vehicle:

options.text: Never the same way twice in a row.
In the same order every time.
Only if you think something is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your vehicle in the same order. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't miss anything.

questions.question: Class 1 hazardous materials are:
questions.explanation: Explosives fall into hazardous materials Class 1.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: Tire failure causes a loud bang or heavy vibration. If steering feels heavy or the rear fishtails, stop and check your tires.

questions.question: When you start the engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:
questions.explanation: Check your gauges when starting the engine. Oil pressure should rise to normal within seconds.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: The driver cannot see behind the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front.
Trailers are not made to go in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver cannot see behind the trailer.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Only back up when absolutely necessary.

questions.question: To use controlled braking, you should:

options.text: Brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep steering movements very small when using this method.

questions.question: If you are unsure your vehicle will fit under a bridge or sign, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under something, slow down and take a different route if possible.

questions.question: After an accident, use flares with caution because:

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares in sunny weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires often happen after accidents because flares are used near spilled fuel. Use flares carefully.

questions.question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:

options.text: Only required when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All vehicles need emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Before each trip, you should inspect your vehicle:

options.text: Never the same way twice in a row.
In the same order every time.
Only if you are unfamiliar with it.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your vehicle in the same order. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't miss anything.

questions.question: In an S-cam brake, friction is created when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: You should use your horn to:

options.text: Tell other drivers that you are angry.
Warn other drivers that you are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers that you are near.
questions.explanation: Your horn warns others of your presence. Use it only when necessary because it can startle other drivers and create danger.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which of the following is NOT required:

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check for adequate power steering fluid.
Ensure that the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure that the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, you must show where the power steering fluid dipstick or sight glass is located and check that the fluid is within a safe range. The fluid should not exceed the full mark.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is on only the tractor, trailer, or one axle, you still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which belt is NOT required to be checked:
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, you may be asked to check the power steering, water pump, alternator, and air compressor belts if your vehicle has them. There is no water compressor belt.

questions.question: The faster you drive:

options.text: The shorter your stopping distance will be.
The longer your stopping distance will be.
The easier it will be to stop your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer your stopping distance will be.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer distances to stop. Adjust your braking accordingly.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must maintain ____ with your vehicle at all times.
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and keep three points of contact while exiting. For buses, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: Which maneuver may be included in the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: Weave between a line of cones.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice that lets you see the road through it. A road covered in black ice may look wet instead of icy. Watch for black ice when roads look wet and temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians do not see you when you pass them. This is an important safety practice.

questions.question: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road, you must:
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, you must put out emergency warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
Only use turn signals if another vehicle is next to you.
Not use a turn signal if the lane change is obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should:
questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must not leak or be broken. A bad exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should check that:

options.text: The grooved pedal surface is not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface is not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing blocks the pedals. Make sure the pedals work properly and the surfaces have grooves to prevent slipping.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained properly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: If you lose your driving privileges:

options.text: The state will tell your employer.
You must tell your employer within two business days.
You must tell your employer within one month.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if you cannot drive.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver ahead, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of space and keep a safe distance.

questions.question: When making a tight turn in a CMV, the driver should:

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Not worry about speed, just focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect a CMV to slow down for a tight turn. Brake early and slow gradually to give them warning.

questions.question: Who is responsible for cargo loaded on a truck?
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for checking the cargo and making sure it is properly secured, even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is normal when a vehicle is warmed up.

questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually so the vehicle does not jerk. Rough acceleration can cause damage to the vehicle.

questions.question: When inspecting the windshield before a trip, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check your windshield for cracks. Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension. Check the wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and to make sure they are secured properly.

questions.question: To avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Braking is always the best option.
Swerving may be more effective than braking.
Drivers should leave 100 yards of distance between their vehicle and the next.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be more effective than braking.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest way to avoid a hazard. You can usually turn to avoid an obstacle faster than you can stop.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, when should you inspect it?

options.text: Only after a trip is finished.
Every time you take a break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break.
questions.explanation: Inspect your cargo and how it is secured every time you take a break. Check it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: A driver who is color blind.
A person who does not know the rules of the road.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have consumed alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are ill are dangerous. One sign of impaired driving is stopping at inappropriate places, such as green traffic lights.

questions.question: If a driver has stopped on the road and is placing warning triangles, how should they hold them?

options.text: Between the driver and oncoming traffic.
Behind the driver's back so other drivers cannot see them until they are placed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between the driver and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, hold warning triangles between your body and oncoming traffic when placing them.

questions.question: How many feet does an air brake vehicle need to stop from 55 mph under good conditions?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under good conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only if you have applied the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When parking on a level surface, use wheel chocks. If your vehicle does not have spring brakes, wheel chocks are essential to prevent the trailer from rolling.

questions.question: Who is responsible for ensuring cargo is loaded properly?
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for four things: inspecting the cargo, checking for overloads and unbalanced weight, ensuring the cargo is secured and does not block vision, and ensuring the cargo does not cover emergency equipment.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signal signs at the crossing and call 911 or the appropriate emergency number.

questions.question: For a triple combination air brake vehicle, the leakage rate in a static leakage test should not exceed ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test for a triple combination air brake vehicle, the leakage rate must not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.
